name: gateway_clamps_priority_and_clips_pixels
description: Art-Net, E1.31, DDP and plain MQTT arrive with no useful authentication, so the bound is enforced at the gateway rather than trusted from the source. A gateway that clamped nothing would turn every Art-Net node on the network into a way to take over a room. Priority is clamped rather than refused - a console sending 255 is a console doing what consoles do, and rejecting the frame leaves a strip dark with no explanation - but out-of-range pixels have no sensible reinterpretation, so they are dropped and counted. The expiry is a bound rather than a value: what the rule requires is that a gateway source always has one, not how long the shell chose to make it.

steps.description: a full Art-Net universe aimed at a 60-pixel binding: two thirds of it is not this gateway's to address, and the priority is far above its ceiling
well inside the binding and under the ceiling, nothing is touched - the clamp must not fire when it is not needed
overlapping the far edge: the part inside is kept and the rest counted, rather than the whole frame being refused
entirely outside it there is nothing to clip to, so it is refused rather than admitted as an empty range
